3_recipe.base: TAUIL ft6k, koine payload geom/day1-9um/select/ckpt/tauil_ft6k.pth (sha256 above): {'model': state_dict, 'config': its training config, 'step'}; built with koine's make_model(config) exactly as day1-select-loaders.py builds it, strict load (0 missing, 0 unexpected, 508 tensors, 68,175,426 parameters). Architecture, normalisation and config unchanged.
3_recipe.input: per sample: depth centre c uniform on the integers -4..+4; the 21-layer slab stack[20 + c - 10 : 20 + c + 11], REVERSED (day 1's rev); window offset o uniform on 0..4; layers [o, o + 17) -> 17 x 128 x 128 render px. Spans layers 6..34 at most, the footprint the 3D cut assumes. Normalised per patch with vesuvius.image_proc.intensity.normalization.normalize_robust, exactly as infer.py's tifxyz_robust path does at inference.
3_recipe.target: the teacher by index (section 1) on the same 128 x 128 px; loss only on TRAINING PX = render mask AND allowed cell AND the scramble twin's rolled-teacher-valid (section 4), so both arms see identical pixels
3_recipe.patches: each step draws 8 windows: a segment with probability proportional to its count of valid window origins, then an origin uniformly among them. A window origin is valid when every px of the window that is inside the render mask is in an allowed cell, and >= 50% of its px are training px.
3_recipe.loss: L = BCE + 0.5 x (1 - rho_hp). BCE = BCEWithLogits(logit, teacher) averaged over training px of the batch: soft targets, label smoothing 0 (the base was trained with 0.5), no pos_weight, no Dice. rho_hp = mean over samples with >= 2048 core px of Pearson(hp(sigmoid(logit)), hp(teacher)) over that sample's core, hp(x) = x - G(x m) / max(G(m), 1e-3), G Gaussian sigma 48 um = 4.994 px (truncate 4 sigma, zero outside the patch), m = training px of the sample, core = m AND G(m, 2 sigma) > 0.999 (day1-score-baselines.py's hp, in-patch). No sample qualifies -> the hp term is 0 that step (counted in the log). Losses in fp32.
3_recipe.optimiser: [machine] AdamW, peak lr 2e-5 (dense_native's fine-tune lr on this architecture, train_dense_native.json), betas (0.9, 0.999), weight decay 3e-5, 500 linear warmup steps from 0 then cosine to 0 at the last step, global grad-norm clip 1.0, no EMA
3_recipe.steps: 12,000 optimiser steps at batch 8 = 96,000 windows, about 1,450 cm2 of window area over 23.05 cm2 allowed, i.e. about 63 passes, chosen to match TAUIL ft6k's own exposure (6,000 steps x 64 windows over roughly 100 cm2 of PHerc0139 is about 58 passes; both the batch, the config's 64, and the 100 cm2 for its 13 segments are assumptions)
3_recipe.precision: bf16 autocast forward on the RTX 4060 8 GB, fp32 master weights and optimiser state; if batch 8 does not fit, 2 micro-batches of 4 with gradient accumulation (same draws, same steps), noted in the log
3_recipe.time_estimate: [machine, unmeasured] day-1 inference ran about 23 windows/s end to end, IO-bound; training forward + backward in memory should take about 0.25-0.9 s per step of 8, so 0.8-3.0 GPU hours per arm (central about 1.7 h) and 1.7-6 h for both arms (central about 3.4 h). If the mean step time over steps 101-300 projects past 6 h for one arm, the run stops and a dated note scales the step count to 4 h for BOTH arms, written before any validation or test number exists. Steps never change for any other reason.
3_recipe.augmentation: spatial, applied to input and target together: mirror each in-plane axis with p 0.5; rot90 in plane by 1, 2 or 3 quarter turns with p 0.3 (koine's default for this patch and rotation axis 0). The depth axis is never flipped or permuted (order carries ink: day 1's forward control scores AUCsup 0.53). Intensity, input only, after normalisation: the intensity members of create_training_transforms from the module koine_machines/data/ink_dataset.py imports, called with no_spatial=True (if that module lacks the flag: koine_machines.augmentation.default_augmentations.create_training_transforms(..., no_spatial=True)). No elastic, scale or translation transform: they would move the letter-scale target against the input.
3_recipe.seed: 20261006 for numpy default_rng (sampling, depth centre, window offset) and torch (augmentation); the SAME seed for the scramble twin, so both arms draw identical windows and augmentations and differ only in targets. Data loading single-process or worker-seeded; cudnn nondeterminism allowed and reported.
3_recipe.early_stopping: NONE. The student is the weights after step 12,000, whatever any curve shows. Checkpoints at 3,000, 6,000 and 9,000 are kept for the log and are never scored on 252405. The validation strip's loss is logged every 2,000 steps and chooses nothing.

6_go.bootstrap: AMENDMENT-1 items 9, 10, 12: 2 mm tiles = 208 x 208 render px anchored at render px (0, 0); a tile enters a metric's pool when it holds >= 1 of that metric's scored px (AUC: a pos or a neg; hp: a core px); 2,000 resamples of the pool with replacement, numpy default_rng(0); T, B and S resampled TOGETHER on the same tiles (pixel multiplicities kept); closure = (S - B) / (T - B) per resample, a resample with T - B <= 0 counts as closure -inf
6_go.G1_AUC_closure: closure on AUCsup: point >= 0.5 AND 2.5th percentile >= 0.25. With B = 0.8102 the point bar is S >= 0.839574 (nAUC >= 0.9204). Always informative here (T - B = 0.0587).
6_go.G2_hp_closure: [machine] closure on hp r at 192 um, blur 2, with the LABEL key K (section 5): point >= 0.5 AND 2.5th percentile >= 0.25. INFORMATIVE only if T_K - B_K >= 2 x the sd of B's 48 rolled-key nulls on core_L (item 8); otherwise UNINFORMATIVE, the hp half is not tested, and GO rests on G1 plus the read (item 8).
6_go.why_G2_uses_the_label_key: [machine] on the ScrollPrize key the teacher IS the key, so T's hp r is its self-correlation (+0.9992), and item 5 would demand S >= 0.3499 + 0.5 x (0.9992 - 0.3499) = 0.6746: half-way to a perfect copy of the 2.4 um map from 9 um data, a bar no reader in the record approaches. Item 5 was written for a teacher distinct from the key (Hecate 2.4 vs the SP key, AMENDMENT-1). The human labels are the one key independent of T, B and S, and AUCsup already uses them. The SP-key literal closure is REPORTED (point and bootstrap), never deciding.

6_go.G4_controls: at 192 um b2: forward, shuffle-21 and shuffle-41 each inside their own nulls (r <= null max, wrap and overlap). At 48 um b2: forward inside its null; shuffle-21 <= max(own null max, 0.0293) and shuffle-41 <= max(own null max, 0.0207), i.e. not more than 0.01 above what the baseline's own shuffles scored (+0.0193, +0.0107). 6_go.G5_scramble_flat: the scramble twin's nAUC <= B's nAUC (as rescored) + 0.02, expected <= 0.8608 (AUCsup <= 0.8176); its hp numbers reported. A twin that gains more is evidence the student's gain is adaptation to the scan, not the teacher's ink, and the verdict is NO-GO.
6_go.G6_letter_read: prereg-v2 notes 2-4 unchanged: reference letter-read/252405-ref.json (8 scorable letters, sha256 above); match = same identity (Reader A's alternatives accepted) with centre within 0.5 mm of Reader A's box centre; GO needs (a) matched >= 6 of 8 (note 2 with the ceiling's m = 6), (b) <= 24 calls on the 25 mirror phase nulls AND <= 24 on the 25 depth-shuffled nulls (the student's own shuffle-21 map, make-pool.py --depth-map), (c) precision >= 0.11; NET, LOCATED, LOCATED-BOX and the tau 0.40 version reported. Pool built like pe: make-pool.py (sha256 above) with the arguments pe used, the student's map and depth map in place of the arm's, --mirror nulls, per_batch 1, FRESH readers who have seen no tile, map or letter of 252405. verdict.GO: G1 AND (G2 pass OR G2 UNINFORMATIVE) AND G3 AND G4 AND G5 AND the twin a valid null AND G6
verdict.NUMBERS GO, LETTER NO-GO: all but G6: the student reads the test better by the gates and still not legibly; NO-GO for a claim
verdict.NO-GO: G1 fails, or G2 informative and fails, or G3, G4 or G5 fails; the letter read is still run and reported (item 6 makes it the decider, so it is never skipped) but cannot turn a gate failure into GO
verdict.INCONCLUSIVE: the twin is not a valid null, or the letter read cannot be run as specified; said, never rounded to GO
verdict.day1_sanity_gates: gates 1 and 2 failed on 252405 on day 1 and depend only on the render and the key, the same for B, T and S; restated in the report, they do not cap this verdict (the closure is relative to B on the same pixels)
